content: Follow your doctor’s instructions for performing breast self-examinations, and report any lumps immediately. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. Managing or preventing high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and diabetes can significantly lower your risk of developing heart disease and experiencing a stroke. Lifestyle modifications that can help control or prevent these conditions include reducing stress, adopting a low-fat and low-salt diet, losing weight if you are overweight, engaging in regular physical activity, and quitting smoking. To help prevent dementia, keep your mind active by engaging in mental exercises such as reading or solving crossword puzzles. For promoting healthy bones, lifestyle changes such as increasing weight-bearing exercises, quitting smoking, limiting alcohol consumption, and eating a well-balanced diet rich in calcium and vitamin D are recommended. Missed Dose Instructions: If you miss a dose of your medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage Instructions: Store the medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information About This Medication: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about the product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Warning About Estrogens: Estrogens, whether used alone or in combination with another hormone (progestin), have been associated with rare but serious side effects. Discuss the risks and benefits of hormone therapy with your doctor. Estrogens can increase the risk of uterine cancer (endometrial cancer). Taking a progestin as directed by your doctor can help reduce this risk. In postmenopausal women, estrogens, with or without progestin, may increase the risk of breast or ovarian cancer, stroke, dementia, and serious blood clots. The risk of these side effects may depend on the dose of estrogen and the duration of use. This medication should be used at the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration necessary. Regularly discuss the use of this medication with your doctor and have periodic check-ups (e.g., every 3 to 6 months) to determine if continued use is necessary. If you are taking this medication long-term, you should undergo regular comprehensive physical exams (e.g., annually) as directed by your doctor. Uses of This Medication: This medication is a hormone (estrogen) used by women to alleviate symptoms of menopause, such as hot flashes and vaginal dryness, which occur due to decreased estrogen production in the body. Certain estrogen products may also be used post-menopause to prevent bone loss (osteoporosis). However, other medications, such as raloxifene or bisphosphonates (e.g., alendronate), may also be effective in preventing bone loss and could be safer alternatives. How to Use This Medication: Read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting this medication and each time you get a refill. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor. If you are using extended-release tablets, do not crush, chew, or dissolve them, as this can release the drug all at once, increasing the risk of side effects. Take this medication regularly to achieve the best results. To help you remember, take it at the same time(s) each day as directed. Follow your dosing schedule carefully. Possible Side Effects: Common side effects may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, bloating, breast tenderness, headache, or weight changes. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause serious (and sometimes fatal) complications from blood clots, such as heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs or legs. Severe allergic reactions to this product are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Avoid smoking or using tobacco. Inform your doctor if you have recently undergone or will undergo surgery, or if you will be confined to a chair or bed for an extended period (e.g., during a long plane flight), as these conditions increase the risk of blood clots, especially if you are taking an estrogen product. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on your face and skin (melasma). Sunlight can worsen this effect, so limit your time in the sun and avoid tanning booths and sunlamps. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug, which could affect their growth and development. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It passes into breast milk and may reduce the quality and quantity of milk produced. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., metyrapone test), potentially causing false test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Regular Monitoring: While taking this medication, you should undergo regular comprehensive physical exams, including laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., blood pressure checks, breast exams/mammograms, pelvic exams, Pap smears). Follow your doctor’s instructions for breast self-examinations and report any lumps immediately. Attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. Lifestyle Recommendations: Preventing or managing high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and diabetes can reduce your risk of heart disease and stroke. Lifestyle changes that can help include reducing stress, eating a low-fat and low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking. To help prevent dementia, engage in mental exercises such as reading or solving puzzles. To promote healthy bones, increase weight-bearing exercises, quit smoking, limit alcohol consumption, and eat a balanced diet with adequate calcium and vitamin D.
